exposure: Type of cesarean section (elective or emergency)
cohort: The study included 42 pregnant patients, comprising 21 scheduled for elective cesarean sections and 21 for emergency cesarean sections, recruited from Prof. RSUP. Dr. R. D. Kandou Hospital Manado and Network Hospital in Manado.
finding: Pregnant patients undergoing emergency cesarean sections exhibited significantly higher cortisol levels and HAM-A anxiety scores compared to those scheduled for elective cesarean sections, and a significant positive correlation was observed between cortisol levels and anxiety levels.
mod_finding: Pregnant patients undergoing emergency cesarean sections showed significantly higher cortisol levels and HAM-A anxiety scores compared to those undergoing elective cesarean sections.
